en: Sutta Nipāta 1.10 Āḷavakasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Āḷavī in the abode of the yakkha Āḷavaka.
Then the yakkha Āḷavaka approached the Blessed One and, having approached, said this to the Blessed One:
“Come out, ascetic!”
“Excellent, friend,” the Blessed One said, and he went out.
“Enter, ascetic,” [the other said].
“Excellent, friend,” the Blessed One said, and he entered.
A second time...
and a third time, the yakkha Āḷavaka said this to the Blessed One:
"Come out, ascetic!"
“Excellent, friend,” the Blessed One said, and he went out.
“Enter, ascetic,” [the other said].
“Excellent, friend,” the Blessed One said, and he entered.
A fourth time, the yakkha Āḷavaka said this to the Blessed One:
“Come out, ascetic!
“I will not come out, friend.”
"Do what you must do. "I shall ask you a question, ascetic.
If you do not answer me, I will either strike your mind, or split your heart, or seize you by the feet and hurl you across the Ganges."
“Friend, I do not see anyone in the world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins,
its gods and humans, who could shake my mind, split my heart, or seize me by the feet and cast me across the Ganges.”
"Moreover, friend, ask whatever you desire.
Then the yakkha Āḷavaka addressed the Blessed One in verse:
"What indeed is the best wealth for a person here?"
What well-performed deed brings happiness?
What indeed is the sweetest of tastes?
How should one live that they call the best way of life?
“Faith is the supreme wealth of a person here;
the Dhamma well-practiced brings happiness;
truth indeed is the sweetest of tastes.”
They say that a life lived with wisdom is the best.
“How indeed does one cross the flood?
How indeed does one cross the ocean?”
"How does one transcend suffering?
How is one thoroughly purified?
"Through faith one crosses the flood."
By heedfulness one crosses the ocean;
by energy one overcomes suffering;
by wisdom one is purified.
“How does one easily obtain wisdom?
How does one easily find wealth?
How does one attain renown?”
How does one bind friends?
How does one go from this world to the next world,
and not grieve after passing away?
“Having faith in the Dhamma of the Arahants for the attainment of Nibbāna,
one gains wisdom through the desire to learn.”
The heedful and discerning one,
who acts appropriately, bears his burden,
and exerts himself, finds wealth.
Through truth one gains renown;
by giving, one binds friends.
For whomsoever these four qualities exist—
For one who has faith and seeks the household life—
truth, the Dhamma, fortitude, and generosity—
he indeed does not grieve after passing away.
Come now, ask others as well—
the many recluses and brahmins—
whether truth, self-control, and generosity [exist].
"Something even greater than patience exists here.
"How indeed should I now question the various recluses and brahmins?"
Today I understand that which is for the sake of the future life;
indeed, it is for my benefit that the Buddha [has appeared].
I have come from the village of Vāsāya;
today I understand that place where what is given bears great fruit.
Thus shall I wander from village to village and from town to town,
paying homage to the Fully Awakened One.
And the true nature of the Dhamma.
The Āḷavaka Sutta, the tenth.
